# The Gravity That Holds Us

## Scripture
"For in him all things were created: things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible... and in him all things hold together." — Colossians 1:16-17

## Reflection
Every autumn, something quietly remarkable happens in the night sky. As the Earth tilts on its axis, the Andromeda Galaxy—our nearest large galactic neighbor—becomes visible to the naked eye from dark locations. A faint smudge of ancient light, it carries over one trillion stars, yet appears smaller than the moon's face.

We tend to think of gravity as a force that pulls things down. But in the vastness of space, gravity is what *holds things together*—binding galaxies, steering planets, keeping a trillion suns from scattering into the void. Andromeda and our own Milky Way are actually hurtling toward each other at 250,000 miles per hour, drawn by an invisible bond neither can resist.

There is a deeper gravity at work in the universe. Paul tells us that Christ Himself is the cosmic glue—the One in whom all things hold together. Not just stars and galaxies, but you and me. When your life feels like it's spinning apart, when anxiety scatters your thoughts and grief pulls you in a hundred directions, you are not free-falling. You are held. The same Word that spoke galaxies into being is the Word that whispers your name.

Look up tonight. Find that faint smudge of light. Let it remind you: the God who holds a trillion stars together holds every fragment of your life.

## Prayer
Lord Jesus, You are before all things and in You all things hold together. When I feel fragmented and scattered, draw me back into Your gravity. Anchor me in Your love. Amen.
